findingDetails.title: Phase 009's completion gate names the run set that failed, not the one that decided it
findingDetails.evidence: Handoff criteria, artifact list, REQ-002 and AC-002 bind scratch/baseline/baseline.json, which holds the first set with run 3 missing_anchors 6; the deciding second fresh set lives at scratch/amend3/fresh2/baseline.json and is named by no requirement or acceptance row.
findingDetails.recommendation: Rebind REQ-002, REQ-004, the artifact row, the handoff criterion and AC-002/AC-004 to the deciding set, or make the report the cited artifact and name the set inside it.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The cited file was parsed (runs[2].missing_anchors 6, seconds 1822), the deciding path read from the report source map, and both requirement and acceptance rows read directly.

claimAdjudication.claim: Phase 009's handoff criterion, artifact list, REQ-002 and AC-002 bind a run file that holds the superseded failing set, while the deciding set's file is named nowhere in the requirements or acceptance criteria.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Searched phase 009 spec.md and acceptance-criteria.md for fresh2, amend3 and second fresh; the only hits are AC-012's status-delta path and the AC footer note, neither a requirement binding.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The packet may intend final runs generically, with the deciding set recorded only as a report amendment. Rejected as sufficient: a Level 3 handoff criterion is the closure gate, and it resolves to an artifact whose numbers contradict the completion claim it gates.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: A requirement, artifact row or acceptance row that names the deciding set's run file as completion evidence, or a handoff criterion rewritten to cite the report instead of a run file.

findingDetails.recommendation: Correct both description.json values from the child spec metadata, and add the ordinal to whatever regeneration writes description.json.
findingDetails.scopeProof: title, Phase row and description.json read for children 007, 008 and 009; 007 agrees and the last two disagree.
